generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this shows up on a single task such as an essay on memory. You might map the theories first, weigh a cognitive and a biological line of argument, and read each study for what its findings could also suggest. The three methods work together on the one piece.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students write the same essay on stress. One lists a few studies and reports them in order. The other maps the theories, drafts two possible arguments and keeps the stronger, then reads each study for links the authors did not draw. The second essay reads as real analysis, because the methods worked together.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, working creatively means using all three methods on one task. You map theories, try more than one argument and adapt, and read studies for what they could also mean. Used together across your modules, they make your psychology work sharper.

check.body: A student plans an essay with a mind map, tries two different arguments, drops the weaker one, and reads each source for what it could mean. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three creative methods are working together as one way of working on a single task.
_items.feedback: Yes. Mapping, flexible thinking and imaginative reading are all in play at once.

_items.text: That the student used only one creative method and ignored the rest.
_items.feedback: Look again: mapping, flexible thinking and imaginative reading all appear.

_items.text: That mind mapping cannot be combined with other methods.
_items.feedback: The example shows mapping combined with the other two methods.

_items.text: That creativity belongs only at the planning stage of an essay.
_items.feedback: Creativity runs on here from planning through to reading the sources.
